front.title: Post-Quantum Hybrid Cryptographic Delegation Chains and Merkle-Aggregated Execution Receipts for Autonomous AI Agents

abstract.t:
Autonomous AI agent ecosystems rely on multi-hop cryptographic delegation chains and signed execution traces (currently built on Ed25519, ECDSA P-256, and RSA-PSS) to enforce least-privilege tool invocations across Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) boundaries, and to preserve long-term non-repudiation for regulatory audit logs. This architecture faces two existential vulnerabilities in the Post-Quantum era: (1) "Harvest-Now, Forge-and- Repudiate-Later" (HNFRL) attacks, wherein Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQCs) running Shor's algorithm retroactively forge or repudiate multi-year compliance traces (e.g., 7-to-10-year HIPAA, SOX, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, and defense operational logs) and synthesize retroactive human-in-the-loop approvals; and (2) "Lattice Signature-Bloat Amplification," wherein naively substituting 64-byte Ed25519 signatures with 3,309-byte ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signatures across a 10-hop sub-agent chain inflates per-call authorization headers from 640 bytes to over 46 KB (including public keys), exceeding HTTP/2 header limits and degrading sub-10ms real-time tool routing.
This document specifies a wire-compatible Post-Quantum Agentic Delegation and Trace Receipt profile ("PQ-Agentic"). It introduces a two-tier cryptographic architecture: (a) a Hot-Path Hybrid Delegation Envelope combining classical Ed25519 with ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) via Pre-Verified Session-Grant Digest Chaining (PVSGDC), replacing redundant per-call inline re-transmission of O(N) prior delegators' 5,261-byte ML-DSA-65 public keys and signatures with 32-byte SHAKE256 digests of out-of-band PEP-verified delegation grants; and (b) a Cold-Path Long-Horizon Archival Receipt anchored with stateless hash- based SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128f (FIPS 205) over RFC 9943 SCITT transparency Merkle roots, guaranteeing 30-year quantum-resistant non-repudiation even under catastrophic lattice cryptanalysis.
